data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["HTTP PUT idempotence is defined by the method specification; event-log append idempotence must be enforced by an out-of-band deduplication mechanism","HTTP PUT targets a named resource with last-write-wins semantics; event-log append targets an unbounded stream where order matters"],"overturn_conditions":["If RFC 9110 \u00a79.2 does not establish the safe \u2282 idempotent hierarchy, the analogy to PUT's classification is unsupported by the cited source"],"shared_structure":["PUT in HTTP: mutates server state, but N identical PUTs leave the resource in the same state as 1 PUT \u2014 idempotent but not safe","Append with idempotency key in event log: mutates log state, but N identical appends leave the log in the same state as 1 append \u2014 idempotent but not safe"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_006"],"transfer_claims":["The PUT\u2194append analogy supports the claim that the event log needs idempotence (PUT-like) rather than safety (GET-like)"]},"claim":"RFC 9110 establishes that safe methods are a proper subset of idempotent methods: a safe method produces no side effects, so repeating it trivially yields the same (null) effect, satisfying idempotence. The converse fails: PUT and DELETE are idempotent but not safe. An append-only event log with at-least-once delivery requires idempotence \u2014 the weaker, more general property \u2014 because writers must mutate state (violating safety) but must not duplicate events under retry (requiring idempotence). Requiring safety would be self-contradictory for a write operation.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If RFC 9110 does not explicitly state or logically imply safe \u2282 idempotent, the subset claim must be presented as inference rather than citation","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the event log's deduplication relies on read-time filtering rather than write-time suppression, the writer itself need not be idempotent \u2014 only the read path must handle duplicates","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The subset relation follows from the definitions: safety means 'no intended state change' (RFC 9110 \u00a79.2.1), and idempotence means 'same intended effect for N requests as for 1' (\u00a79.2.2). If the effect of one request is 'no state change,' then the effect of N requests is also 'no state change,' so safe \u27f9 idempotent. The event-log writer's append is a mutation (not safe) but must be designed to converge under repetition (idempotent). This places it squarely in the idempotent-but-not-safe region, alongside HTTP PUT.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
